chunks: And their leading chiefs said: 'Remain attached to your gods. There is surely some motive behind it.'

key_terms.الْمَلَأُ: The elite, chiefs, or prominent leaders
key_terms.شَيْءٌ يُرَادُ: A thing/motive intended (implying a calculated plan or ulterior motive)

ai.seo_question: What did the chiefs of Hud's people say to keep their followers loyal to their idols?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse illustrates the 'elite' (al-mala') who, despite recognizing the truth, prioritized social cohesion and political stability over spiritual conviction, viewing Hud's call as a disruptive social experiment. Their command to 'walk and be patient' reflects a strategy of passive endurance rather than active rejection, aiming to preserve the existing idolatrous order by attributing the Prophet's mission to mere human ambition. This dynamic underscores the recurring theme of the powerful suppressing divine truth to maintain their hegemony.
